questions.question: In a patient with progressive thrombocytopenia after cardiopulmonary bypass, what clinical features and timing would increase your suspicion for heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT), and how can recent preoperative heparin exposure shift the onset earlier than the usual postoperative day 5–10 window?
How does autoimmune HIT (aHIT) differ from classic HIT in terms of antibody behavior and platelet activation, and what serotonin-release assay (SRA) findings support a diagnosis of aHIT?

A postoperative patient has a strong-positive PF4/polyanion ELISA but an ‘indeterminate’ SRA because serotonin release persists despite FcγRIIa blockade (IV.3). How should this result be interpreted, and what diagnosis does it suggest in the appropriate clinical context?
List at least five alternative causes of severe thrombocytopenia in the early post–cardiac surgery period and explain which clinical or laboratory findings in this case help exclude each one.

What is the rationale for initiating argatroban rather than therapeutic-dose fondaparinux as first-line anticoagulation in a patient with suspected aHIT complicated by acute ischemic stroke and profound thrombocytopenia, and why was a subsequent switch to fondaparinux reasonable?

Describe the mechanism by which high-dose intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) mitigates thrombocytopenia and thrombosis in aHIT, and provide plausible reasons why a patient might show only a modest platelet response to IVIG.

Which laboratory markers can be followed to gauge HIT-associated hypercoagulability and consumptive coagulopathy during treatment, and how did trends in fibrinogen, d-dimer, and schistocytes inform management in this case?
When using fondaparinux for treatment of HIT, under what circumstances should antithrombin supplementation be considered, and what is the physiological basis for this strategy?

What SRA pattern distinguishes HIT antibodies from nonspecific platelet activation at varying heparin concentrations, and why does absence of release at very high heparin levels (e.g., 100 U/mL) support HIT antibody specificity?
